questions.question: The best way to stop quickly is to:

options.text: Use the front brake only.
Use the rear brake first.
Close the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time. Press the brakes firmly. Do not panic if the brakes lock.

questions.question: To stop in the shortest distance in a straight line:

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes and lock the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: On a straightaway, use both brakes to stop in the shortest distance. Try not to lock either brake.

questions.question: When a tire goes flat, the rider can often hear it.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: You will rarely hear a tire go flat. Instead, you may notice the motorcycle handles differently when a tire fails.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Relax, keep your speed steady, and ride straight across.
Hold the handlebars tighter and speed up to pass the hazard.
Ride in a zigzag pattern.
Ride on the shoulder instead of the grooves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep your speed steady, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is usually not dangerous. If this happens, relax and ride straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.
Only protects your eyes.
Protects your whole face.
Is not as good as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield helps protect your whole face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield cannot replace goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride on the right side of the lane.
Move across the lane as the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Riding on the side near the passing vehicle increases the risk of a crash. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: To discourage other vehicles from sharing your lane:

options.text: Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride in the center of the lane.
Make eye contact and give angry looks.
Ride in a zigzag pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to stop other drivers from trying to squeeze in next to you.

questions.question: If you accidentally lock your rear wheel while braking on good pavement:

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and apply it again quickly.
Release the rear brake and downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If you lock the rear brake on good pavement, keep it locked until you stop. You can still control your motorcycle if it is upright and going straight.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time to a hazard, you should:

options.text: Always ride below the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready near the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready near the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to a hazard.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Speed up to stop the wobble.
Brake immediately.
Grip the handlebars tight and slowly close the throttle.
Downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars tight and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble because this makes it worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle to slow down. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as possible. Do not brake, as this may make the wobble worse.

questions.question: What formation should riders use when going through curves, making turns, or entering a highway?

options.text: Pairs.
Single-file.
Staggered.
Passing.

questions.explanation: Use single-file formation when riding through curves, turns, or entering or exiting a highway. Staggered formation is best on straight roads, but not in these situations.

questions.question: During a normal turn, how should the motorcycle and rider position themselves?

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should lean, but the rider should not.
The rider should lean, but the motorcycle should not.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
questions.explanation: During a normal turn, the motorcycle and rider lean at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?

options.text: About one-quarter
About one-half
About three-quarters

questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Where in a lane should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: Always avoid the left portion of a lane.
Always avoid the right portion of a lane.
Always avoid the center portion of a lane.
Use whichever portion of the lane is safest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use whichever portion of the lane is safest.
questions.explanation: There is no single lane position to always avoid. Change your position based on road conditions.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group ride?

options.text: In the front of the group.
Right behind the leader.
At the back of the group.
Wherever they are most comfortable.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride right behind the leader near the front. This lets experienced riders at the back watch them and help if needed.
